requirement:
> `Inspect a known node's outgoing targets for the requested label, making those
> targets available to read_node.`
rationale:
**Confirmation:** the assessments disagreed

First assessment `true`: structural: The requirement `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.outgoing_edges.mcp.description` quotes only the description string of the `outgoing_edges` MCP tool: "Inspect a known node's outgoing targets for the requested label, making those targets available to read_node." It names no library, algorithm, signature, type, field or delegation. Only the observable description text is required. A different implementation could build the tool definition another way, such as a constant or a derive, and still advertise the same text. How it is built is therefore discretionary, and no structural obligation needs implementation evidence.

The supplied root, `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tools.rs#impl[GraphSession<'_, '_, D>/Conversation]/fn[tools]`, does produce the text. Its `outgoing_edges` tool definition carries the exact description string, so the observable behavior is met. No missing root or gap was found.

behavioral: `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.outgoing_edges.mcp.description` only fixes the text of the `outgoing_edges` tool description: "Inspect a known node's outgoing targets for the requested label, making those targets available to read_node." It has no MUST, MUST NOT or SHOULD clause about runtime behavior. The requirement has no test edges, and I found no test that asserts this description.

The only carrier is a fixed string literal in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tools.rs#impl[GraphSession<'_, '_, D>/Conversation]/fn[tools]`. That literal sits in a `json!` object with no conditional and no transformation of its own. The only branch in the function is for extra domain tools, and it does not touch this description. The testing criteria exempt an obligation carried out by code like this. A test would only compare the literal with a copy of itself.

The effect the description names is that read_node can then be used on the returned targets. That is behavior of the `outgoing_edges` tool, not of the description text. It belongs to the requirements that govern the tool, and I did not assess it here.

The existing tests do not assert the description text. They check tool names and parameter schemas: `agent/configured.rs#mod[tests]/fn[registered_tools_use_the_current_context_and_ordinary_node_ids]`, `agent/tests.rs#fn[default_tool_accepts_scalar_results_and_keeps_the_exact_prefix]` and `agent/tests.rs#fn[graph_tools_record_delivered_snapshots_and_prepared_pages_do_not_record_delivery]`. That is acceptable for a constant string.

I found no obligation here that lacks test evidence.

Second assessment `false`: Add a test, for example in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs` next to `default_tool_accepts_scalar_results_and_keeps_the_exact_prefix`. It should capture the tool list sent to the provider. It should find the tool named `outgoing_edges` and assert that its `description` equals exactly "Inspect a known node's outgoing targets for the requested label, making those targets available to read_node.". Then mark that test with {test}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.outgoing_edges.mcp.description`. — The requirement fixes the exact description text of the `outgoing_edges` tool. The requirement has no {test} edges. The only code that carries the string is `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tools.rs#impl[GraphSession<'_, '_, D>/Conversation]/fn[tools]`. Existing tests check the tool names, the parameter schemas and the call behavior of `outgoing_edges`. These are `default_tool_accepts_scalar_results_and_keeps_the_exact_prefix`, `agent_edge_tools_record_selections_without_validating_targets`, `edge_and_outline_tools_accept_source_addresses_and_domain_data` and `registered_tools_use_the_current_context_and_ordinary_node_ids`. The last of these asserts the `description` only for `lookup_requirements`. A search for `.description`, `["description"]` and the phrase "targets available" found no assertion on the `outgoing_edges` description. The string is a literal inside a `json!` value, so the exemption for pass-through values does not apply. The check would change the description in any way, such as a reworded or truncated sentence, and the existing tests would still pass.

Recorded the second assessment (`false`).
